clue.text: In play Viola's stopped by a knight in the country

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are plugged partway through by the next pieces, as a hole is stopped
letters at play are loose and free to move, so the name Viola's is shuffled

parts.note: the name Viola with its S, all six letters used
K is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: Viola, the heroine of a Shakespeare comedy, is interrupted on stage by a knight somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' looks like 'in a play', placing Viola on stage; it is the anagram signal, and 'stopped by' plugs the shuffled letters with A and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain example: Slovakia is a central European nation, the eastern half of former Czechoslovakia.

clue.text: Cast getting hold of adult books in poor condition

indicators.note: getting hold of means the throw word grips the other letters within it

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
B is short for book, doubled for books

explanation.surface: A theatre cast keeps hold of grown-up reading material that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors; it is the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby means worn and tatty, in poor repair, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Solitary individual old pub's managed without

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the verb surrounds the pub abbreviation

parts.note: ran a business is managed it
PH, public house, is short for pub

explanation.surface: A lonely figure goes without the old pub he once ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A child with no parents is left alone in the world, a solitary individual by loss.

clue.text: I'm nature's fluid remedy for disease

indicators.note: fluid means liquid and shifting, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast from a liquid tonic: I am nature's own cure for illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' looks like part of the description of a liquid medicine, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiserum is blood serum carrying antibodies, given to treat or protect against an infection.

clue.text: Confused in calling the French "Dutch"

parts.note: terming is calling something by a name
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone muddled is calling the French people Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermingled means mixed together, jumbled up, which is one sense of confused.

clue.text: Cattle food from trough changing hands

indicators.note: right hand is swapped for left hand, so an R gives way to an L

parts.note: a manger is a feeding trough for animals

explanation.surface: Fodder is moved from one trough to another as it passes between farmhands.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are the usual shorthand for right and left (hands).
explanation.definitionFit: A mangel, or mangel-wurzel, is a large beet grown as winter fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Unpalatable fruit or a cereal?

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A question of classification: is this bitter thing a fruit or a grain?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the nut into 'a corn'.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak, bitter and not good to eat raw, so an inedible fruit.

clue.text: Dignity — informer briefly clutches Bible with it

indicators.note: clutches means holds tight within, so the shortened word surrounds the rest
briefly means cut short, so the informer word loses its last letter

parts.note: a grass is slang for a police informer
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police informant clings to a Bible to appear respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas is serious, weighty bearing, a synonym of dignity.

clue.text: Production of Cats, say, editor covered haphazardly

parts.note: a litter is the brood of kittens a cat produces

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor reviews a production of the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Production of Cats' suggests the stage musical; here it is a cat's litter of kittens.
explanation.definitionFit: Littered means strewn with scattered things, untidily spread over.

clue.text: Father takes turn with little inclination

indicators.note: the word for father turns round, reading the other way

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A dad takes his turn at something along with a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a desire or liking for something, so it serves as a synonym for inclination.

clue.text: Hollywood star, one of 12 drinking G&T

indicators.note: the farm animal takes in the drink's first letter, swallowing it

parts.note: 12 across is BOARS, so one of them is a single boar
the G of the gin and tonic
the T of the gin and tonic, which follows

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star, in a pigsty with the 12-across animals, knocks back a gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: The boar swallows only the G of the drink; the T trails after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a leading American film actor, star of Casablanca, so he is an example of a Hollywood star.

clue.text: Go into care managed by an oldie

indicators.note: managed means handled or worked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person goes into residential care, arranged on their behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: An octogenarian is someone in their eighties, certainly an elderly person.

clue.text: Fastens covers over farm animals

indicators.note: the verb for fastening goes over the outside of the cricket letter, covering it

parts.note: to bar a door is to fasten it, so bars means fastens
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A farmer fastens covers over the livestock to protect them.
explanation.definitionFit: Boars are uncastrated male pigs kept on farms for breeding, so farm animals fits.

clue.text: One circle converted to square

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these nine letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: turning a circle into a square, the classic impossible problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like the shape, part of the geometry; here it is the verb meaning settle or make agree.
explanation.definitionFit: To square two accounts or views is to reconcile them, make them agree.

clue.text: Characteristic step heard after troops' second entry into the Tower

indicators.note: after places the spoken piece behind the soldiers and the second

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: heard says the word for step is spoken, and its twin in sound is written down

parts.note: a gait is a manner of stepping or walking

explanation.surface: A distinctive marching step is heard as soldiers follow up with a second entry into the Tower of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Traitors' Gate is the river gate of the Tower of London, through which prisoners were brought by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the specific named gateway through which the condemned entered the Tower, a defining example.

clue.text: Nasty smells on the rise until most of mug dried out

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: BO, body odour, plural BOs, means nasty smells
ere is an old word for before, until

indicators.note: most of means the word drops its final letter

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a dupe

explanation.surface: Bad odours rise from a cup until most of it has evaporated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' is a cup in the picture but a fool in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dried out is to stop being drunk, the phrasal verb used here as a past tense.

clue.text: Frisked about and drove cat wild

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters run free and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frolicked about and drove the cat crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap or caper about playfully, so a past-tense synonym of frisked about.

clue.text: What choirs do about sound of violent shoving?

indicators.note: about means around, so the singing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: choirs sing

indicators.note: sound of means the word for violent is said aloud and written as its soundalike

parts.note: tough can mean violent or rough

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about why choirs sing about rough jostling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'shoving' is stuffing in the sense of cramming in, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing is cramming or forcing things in, roughly the same as shoving them in.

clue.text: 10 asked for it in due course

definitions.meaning: 10 across is Bogart; in Casablanca his character asks Sam to play this song

explanation.surface: Bogart in Casablanca asked Sam to play the song, and time passed.
explanation.walkthrough: The song of Casablanca's famous 'Play it, Sam' scene is used as the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, gradually over time, which matches in due course as an idiom.

clue.text: Officer giving orders to tie up chicken

parts.note: CO, commanding officer, is the officer who gives orders

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a draw is a tied game

explanation.surface: An officer orders someone to truss up a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the bird to be trussed; here it means a cowardly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a timid person lacking courage, a direct synonym.

clue.text: US city depressed everyone coming in from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read from the bottom up, backwards
coming in puts the everyone word inside the word for low spirits

parts.note: sad means low, depressed
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone arriving in an American city from the south is downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a major city in Texas, an example of a US city.

clue.text: Summary of artist's stage exit is not recorded

parts.note: leaving the stage is coming off; in short form, 'off came'
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A brief report on a performer walking offstage says the moment went unfilmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summary of' asks for the headline version of 'the artist came off stage': OFF CAME RA, the words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening off camera is outside the filming, so it is not caught on tape.

clue.text: Wife leaves deviously to get fish

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the wife letter departs from the word

parts.note: to wangle is to get something by cunning

explanation.surface: A wife sneaks off to buy some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun at the end; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with a rod and line, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Little woman in song knocked back wine

indicators.note: knocked back reads the assembled letters backwards, like a drink downed
in places the girl's name inside the word for a tune

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A small woman in the middle of singing downs a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Spanish region of the same name, so it is an example of wine.

clue.text: Urgency ranking, say, overturned after short hearing

indicators.note: after puts the turned abbreviation behind the shortened hearing
short means the word for a court hearing loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in court

indicators.note: overturned turns the abbreviation upside down, here read backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: An urgent case's ranking is overturned after a brief court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' and 'hearing' suggest an appeal court, but they work separately: 'overturned' reverses EG to GE, 'short' cuts TRIAL to TRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Triage is the sorting of patients by how urgently they need treatment, a ranking of urgency.

clue.text: Snake's come a cropper, an unexpected bonus

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a road winds
to come a cropper is to fall heavily

explanation.surface: A snake takes a tumble, which somebody counts as a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'come a cropper' is British slang for to have a bad fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is fruit blown down by wind, and figuratively an unlooked-for gain of money.

clue.text: Player of course could find it tricky to follow on

definitions.text: Player of course could find it tricky

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A cricketer forced to follow on finds the second innings tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow on' is a cricket term, misleading here; 'course' is a golf course, whose bending holes are doglegs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a golf hole that bends sharply, a well-known challenge for a golfer.

clue.text: Definitely trendy equipment for use in bed

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
spades are tools for digging a garden bed

explanation.surface: A shopping claim: this fashionable kit is a must for the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not a sleeper's; the tools are garden spades.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom in spades means in large measure, emphatically, so it carries the sense of definitely.
